questions.stem: An eventstream must drop events whose temperature is below zero before they reach the destination, without code. What do you add?

options.text: A new workspace for the below-zero events
A KQL update policy on the source
A Notebook activity in a pipeline
A Filter operation in the eventstream

questions.explanation: The eventstream editor has no-code operations such as Filter between the source and destinations.

questions.stem: The same stream must reach an eventhouse for live queries and a lakehouse for history. How do you set this up?

options.text: Add both as destinations of the one eventstream
Create two event hubs and send the data twice from the devices
Copy the eventhouse to the lakehouse every night with a pipeline
It isn't possible; an eventstream has one destination

questions.explanation: An eventstream can send its events, or processed versions of them, to several destinations at once.

questions.stem: Which three are no-code operations you can add in an eventstream? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Manage fields
Group by
Call a stored procedure
Filter
Run a Python script

questions.explanation: The event processor offers operations such as Filter, Manage fields, Aggregate, Group by, Union, Expand and Join. Scripts and stored procedures aren't eventstream operations.

questions.stem: Put the steps of setting up a new eventstream in order.

options.text: Add a source
Add a destination
Publish the eventstream
Create the eventstream
Add any processing operations

questions.explanation: You create the eventstream, connect a source, then connect destinations and add processing operations (an operator can also be inserted on the line between a source and a destination you already added), and publish so the changes take effect and the eventstream returns to Live view.

questions.stem: An eventstream uses a Union operator to combine a stream that has DeviceId, Temp and Site with a stream that has DeviceId, Temp and Region. Which fields reach the output?

options.text: All fields from the first input only
No fields, because Union requires identical schemas
DeviceId and Temp only
DeviceId, Temp, Site and Region, with nulls where a field is missing

questions.explanation: Union keeps fields with the same name and data type; fields that don't match are dropped.

questions.stem: Each event in an eventstream has an array of readings, and the destination table needs one row per reading. Which operator should you add?

options.text: Group by
Union
Manage fields
Expand

questions.explanation: Expand creates a new row for each value in an array. Manage fields changes columns, Group by aggregates, and Union combines streams.

questions.stem: You add a Filter operator in an eventstream and want to send its output to a destination that doesn't support adding operators before ingestion. What should you do?

options.text: Connect the destination directly to the default stream
Replace the Filter operator with a SQL operator on the destination
Add a derived stream as the operator's output and attach the destination to it
Move the Filter operator after the destination node

questions.explanation: For destinations without pre-ingestion operators, output the operator to a derived stream and append the destination to it.

questions.stem: You add a Manage fields operator between a stream and a lakehouse destination in an existing eventstream. Put the steps in order.

options.text: Select Publish to return to Live view
Select Refresh to validate the test result
Connect the stream to the operator and the operator to the destination
Select Edit on the ribbon to enter Edit mode
Hover over the connection line, select +, and choose Manage fields
Select the output fields in the Manage fields pane

questions.explanation: You edit, insert the operator, reconnect the nodes, configure it, check the test result, and then publish.

questions.stem: You plan to use a SQL operator in an eventstream. Which two statements are true? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: You can chain several SQL operators in one path to split complex logic
It supports only lakehouse destinations
It works with any eventstream name, including names with dots
You can't combine it with other built-in operators in the same processing path
You must create new destination nodes for it instead of reusing existing ones

questions.explanation: The SQL operator can't be mixed with other operators or chained in one path, and it needs new destination nodes. It supports all Real-Time Intelligence destinations, and names with an underscore or dot aren't compatible.

questions.stem: An eventstream must calculate the average and maximum temperature per device over each 5-minute period, with options for different time windows. Which no-code operator fits?

options.text: Aggregate
Group by
Manage fields
Expand

questions.explanation: Group by calculates aggregations across all events in a time window and has more window options. Aggregate updates a running aggregation every time a new event occurs.
